care_team_notes: Start planning discussions early while communication and decision-making capacity are strong; involve the MND advisor, GP, neurologist, palliative care team, family and chosen decision-maker.
description: MND-specific planning guidance covering advance care planning, substitute decision-makers, wills, finances, palliative care, voluntary assisted dying, personal wishes and changing future needs.
name: Planning ahead with MND

care_team_notes: Refer early to palliative care and review periodically; do not wait until a crisis or severe communication difficulty before discussing preferences and likely future scenarios.
description: MND-specific professional guidance on early referral to specialist palliative care, end-of-life conversations, symptom planning, family support and coordinated multidisciplinary care.
name: End of life care in MND

care_team_notes: Check the correct state or territory form, confirm capacity and witnessing requirements, and upload or share documents with family, substitute decision-maker, GP and treating services.
description: Australian guidance on values, preferences, future healthcare decisions, advance care directives, substitute decision-makers, state and territory legal differences and sharing documents.
name: Advance care planning
publisher: Healthdirect Australia / Advance Care Planning Australia

care_team_notes: Explain that palliative care can be added alongside active MND management and may help with symptoms, planning, equipment, family support and preferred place of care.
description: General Australian information on palliative care, quality of life, symptom management, emotional/social/spiritual support, family and carer support, and finding services.
name: Palliative care overview
publisher: Healthdirect Australia / Palliative Care Australia / CareSearch

care_team_notes: For legal questions, use jurisdiction-specific resources and encourage legal/clinical advice; clinicians should document decision-making capacity, preferences and decision-maker authority.
description: Australian legal toolkit covering capacity, consent, advance care directives, substitute decision-making, withholding or withdrawing life-sustaining treatment, pain relief, disputes and voluntary assisted dying.
name: End-of-life law and substitute decision-making

care_team_notes: Before home death is likely, ensure family know who to call, where documents are kept, what changes to expect, medicine/equipment plans and when urgent help is needed.
description: Australian information for families and carers about preparing for an expected home death, who to contact, death certification, documents, grief and practical next steps.
name: Preparing for an expected death at home

care_team_notes: Always select forms by the person's state or territory and review current witnessing/signing requirements before completion.
description: Jurisdiction-specific advance care planning and directive forms, including examples from Queensland and Victoria, with different rules for appointment, witnessing and legal effect.
name: State and territory advance care planning forms
publisher: Advance Care Planning Australia / state governments
